account: Researchers randomly assigned 147 schools in seven U.S. states to Cognitive Tutor Algebra I or their usual curriculum during the 2007–08 and 2008–09 school years. The program combined classroom teaching, materials, and adaptive tutoring. The revised analysis included 11,066 high-school students and 5,519 middle-school students. It estimated a gain of 0.21 standard deviations for the second high-school cohort. First-year and middle-school results were not statistically significant. The revised What Works Clearinghouse review found that the second-year result also failed its corrected significance threshold. Each year involved a new cohort, rather than a second year of exposure for the same students.

ai_role.statement: The tutor provided adaptive exercises and feedback within a complete algebra curriculum. The trial did not separate its contribution from classroom teaching, materials, or training.
